articles.headlineTranslated: Beware of a measles outbreak; parents reminded to complete their children's vaccinations before homecoming travel.
articles.summary: Indonesia's IDAI warns parents traveling for 2026 Mudik that measles outbreaks keep the country second worldwide in Kejadian Luar Biasa (KLB). Ensure children receive complete basic immunization, especially Measles-Rubella (MR) or Measles, Mumps, Rubella (MMR) vaccines, before departure. Beyond measles, crowded transport increases risk of coughs and colds; recommend masking in public spaces and on transport, and teaching children to cover coughs/sneezes with tissue or elbow and not sharing utensils. For Mudik preparedness, IDAI suggests including an essential medicines list in the homecoming first-aid kit, avoiding overly crowded tourist sites, and favoring controlled educational venues like museums, science centers, or libraries. Also monitor weather and avoid flood or landslide-prone areas for child safety. These reminders come as Indonesia faces ongoing measles outbreak concerns as of March 19, 2026.

articles.headlineTranslated: IDAI Shares Tips for Safe Mudik to Protect Children from Infectious Diseases
articles.summary: IDAI (Indonesian Pediatric Association) urges safer mudik for children amid Indonesia's measles concerns. As of 19 March 2026 in Jakarta, IDAI president Piprim Basarah Yanuarso advises avoiding crowded venues, keeping distance from people with coughs or colds, and practicing PHBS—handwashing with soap and running water—plus carrying hand sanitizer; masks in transit or public spaces provide extra protection. Teach children cough and sneeze etiquette and avoid sharing utensils or drinking bottles. Ensure complete immunization before mudik, especially measles-rubella (MR) or measles, mumps, rubella (MMR) vaccines, given ongoing measles outbreaks (KLB) in Indonesia. Prefer safe, educational destinations (museums, science centers, libraries); avoid disaster-prone areas and extreme weather. Prepare a travel kit: family first aid, fever reducers, oral rehydration salts, bandages, documents, tickets, emergency hospital numbers, plus jackets, rain gear, spare clothes, and healthy snacks.

articles.headline: Heading to Bali, Vietnam or Thailand? Why a measles vaccine is more important than ever
articles.summary: Measles outbreaks persist in Bali, Vietnam, and Thailand, prompting Australian authorities to stress vaccination ahead of travel. From Jan 2025 to Mar 2026, Australia recorded 60 measles infections: 34 acquired overseas and 26 locally acquired; 18 linked to an imported case, eight with no clear source, indicating community transmission. Indonesia ranked third in CDC’s outbreaks by Feb 2026; measles is endemic in Thailand, with rising activity in Vietnam. Measles spreads by airborne particles up to two hours and is contagious from four days before to four days after rash. Early flu-like symptoms precede a rash; complications include pneumonia, otitis media, and encephalitis; fatality about 1–3 per 1,000 in high-income settings. Herd immunity around 95%. In Australia, 2024 first-dose at 12 months was 94.7% and 18-month second-dose 89.5%. Vaccination, including a six-month infant dose for travelers, should be at least two weeks before departure.

articles.headlineTranslated: Don't Touch Babies Carelessly During Eid al-Fitr: Risks of Disease Transmission and How to Prevent Them
articles.summary: Measles transmission risk during Eid al-Fitr gatherings in Indonesia rises from close contact with babies and toddlers. The Indonesian Ministry of Health official, Acting Director General for Disease Control Andi Saguni, warns that touching infants during Lebaran should be reduced or avoided due to high transmission risk, since large family gatherings can accelerate spread and babies are highly vulnerable. In addition to touching, kissing babies also poses infection routes. UK family doctor Dr. Sermed Mezher notes that kissing a baby's face or lips can spread infections; many pediatricians endorse a 'no kissing' policy for anyone other than the primary caregiver, especially on the face or hands. If a child develops fever or a red rash suggesting measles, seek medical care promptly and avoid gatherings. HSV-1 herpes simplex can also be transmitted via close contact like kissing or skin-to-skin contact.

articles.summary: Measles outbreaks persist in Southeast Asia, Bali, Vietnam, and Thailand, as of February 2026. Australian health authorities warn overseas travel drives cases, with New South Wales reporting 60 infections in 2025–26; 34 acquired overseas, 18 linked to a known imported case, eight with no clear source. Indonesia remains a major source and ranks third in the CDC’s outbreak list; Vietnam shows rising activity and Thailand remains endemic, with transmission up since 2023. The National Immunisation Program provides free vaccines at 12 and 18 months; a 6-month early dose is available for traveling infants. Adults born 1966+ without two doses should consider vaccination. Two doses protect about 99%.

articles.summary: Measles complications threaten children as Indonesia reports rising cases from 2025 into early 2026. Although often seen as mild, measles can trigger pneumonia, severe dehydration, and encephalitis in affected children. The Jakarta-based report (ANTARA) ties the upsurge to ongoing transmission across Indonesia, with cases climbing through 2025 and into early 2026. Dr. Venty, Sp.A, CIMI, a pediatrician at Bethsaida Hospital in Gading Serpong, warns that risk is highest among unvaccinated children or those with weakened immune systems. The article does not provide specific laboratory-confirmed case counts. Emphasis is placed on vaccination and timely care to prevent serious outcomes, underscoring the need for continued public health vigilance as measles activity persists nationwide during 2025–early 2026.

articles.headlineTranslated: Beware of a surge in measles cases in Indonesia: Recognize the symptoms, risks, and the importance of vaccination.
articles.summary: Measles surges in Indonesia persist, with 11,094 laboratory-confirmed cases and 69 deaths in 2025, and 572 cases with 4 deaths through week 7 of 2026. Dr. Regina Satya Wiraharja warns of higher transmission during social celebrations. Measles is a contagious RNA virus from Paramyxoviridae, spread by droplets and contaminated surfaces; the virus can linger in air and on objects for hours. Incubation is 8–14 days. Early symptoms include high fever, malaise, runny nose, cough, photophobia, and Koplik spots, with a rash typically starting near the ears/face and spreading over 6–7 days. At-risk groups include young children, immunocompromised individuals, and pregnant women (risk of miscarriage, preterm birth, low birth weight). Complications include pneumonia, severe diarrhea with dehydration, otitis, and encephalitis. Vaccination with MMR remains the most effective control; Indonesia recommends three measles vaccine doses alongside PHBS. If symptoms appear, seek care and limit contact.

articles.headline: Predicting epidemics through genomic analysis of wastewater | The University of Tokyo
articles.summary: Genome analysis of domestic wastewater in Japan, at the University of Tokyo, led by Associate Professor Shinobu Kazama, aims to predict epidemics by detecting human enteric viruses such as norovirus. Using next-generation sequencing, most detected genomes infect bacteria like E. coli or plants, with human enteric viruses comprising only a subset, suggesting low detection probability. A selective detection approach identified known human viruses; ICTV lists over 9,000 virus species, and 62% of detected genomes were not registered in public databases, implying potential unknown viruses. An epidemic indicator using wastewater to estimate norovirus cases is being developed, though regional rainfall and industrial wastewater complicate interpretation. Incomplete virus removal at treatment plants risks discharge into rivers and accumulation in shellfish. Indonesian project in Yogyakarta investigates groundwater fecal contamination from wells and backyard poultry to improve water environments and wastewater research.

articles.headline: Mikroplastik Jadi Kendaraan Berbahaya bagi Bakteri Patogen dan Gen Kebal Antibiotik
articles.headlineTranslated: Microplastics Become a Dangerous Vehicle for Pathogenic Bacteria and Antibiotic Resistance Genes
articles.summary: Microplastics act as a dangerous vehicle for pathogenic bacteria and antibiotic resistance genes, enabling spread from hospital waste to the open sea. In a study by Plymouth Marine Laboratory and the University of Exeter, microplastics rapidly acquire a dense microbial biofilm, the Plastisphere, providing a habitat for disease-causing bacteria. The researchers deployed plastic beads, polystyrene, wood, and glass along a pollution pathway from hospital wastewater to downstream rivers and marine waters. Bacterial densities were highest at hospital effluent, but downstream and marine environments showed elevated antibiotic resistance gene loads on plastics—far exceeding natural materials such as wood or glass. Bacteria such as Flavobacteriia and Vibrio increased on plastic biofilms in downstream regions, organisms known to cause disease in fish and humans and threaten seafood safety in aquaculture zones. The study calls for improved waste management and cross-sector strategies, and recommends gloves and handwashing for beach-cleanup volunteers to reduce exposure.

articles.headline: A New Front Line: How AI And Other Innovations Are Transforming The Fight Against TB
articles.summary: AI-powered handheld digital X-ray devices enable high-volume TB screening with AI analysis, already in use in over 22 countries funded by the Global Fund. Coupled with molecular diagnostics and battery-powered devices, this accelerates diagnosis, aiming to reach the roughly 2.5 million people with active TB who are never diagnosed. Indonesia exemplifies scalable rollout: over 460 local puskesmas now initiate treatment, and private clinics and pharmacies are engaged to extend reach through public-private partnerships. Globally, about 20% of people harbor latent TB; activation risks rise with HIV, malnutrition, smoking, diabetes. Distinguishing drug-sensitive from drug-resistant TB remains critical. Advances include better latent TB treatments and a likely TB vaccine by 2029. Health ministries must tailor intervention mixes to local epidemiology; the Global Fund supports funding decisions, while AI could inform policy and prioritization amid under-resourced efforts on World TB Day.

articles.summary: Measles cases in Yogyakarta, Indonesia, have surged ahead of Eid al-Fitr 2026, with 73 laboratory-confirmed cases through week 9 of 2026, about 5.6-fold higher than the same period in 2025. The most affected are children aged 2–9 years, with newborns under 9 months also affected before vaccination eligibility. Dr. Ari Kurniawati notes the vaccination gap: MR1 coverage in Yogyakarta exceeds 95%, but MR2 stands around 90%, potentially weakening herd immunity over the next five years. Health officials caution against panic but urge travelers to plan carefully, especially when accompanying vulnerable groups such as infants; monitor spread and avoid crowds if not essential. Transmission is often within households and may be mistaken for other febrile illnesses (e.g., dengue); when unwell, wear masks and limit contact to reduce spread.

articles.headlineTranslated: Preventing Measles Transmission During Mudik
articles.summary: Measles remains a public-health concern during the Lebaran mudik travel season in Indonesia. Primary prevention relies on MR/MMR vaccination with a booster at ages 5–7. General measures include handwashing with soap, proper cough etiquette, and isolating infected individuals. Transmission occurs via respiratory droplets, and the virus can linger in air or on surfaces. Complications can be severe or fatal, especially in unvaccinated or immunocompromised children. Early symptoms resemble flu, with high fever and the 3 Cs—cough, coryza, conjunctivitis—often with Koplik spots appearing 1–2 days before the rash. The rash starts on the head/behind the ears and spreads downward, changing from pale red to dark red. There is no specific antiviral; management is supportive (rest, fluids, nutrition) and vitamin A for two consecutive days per age-appropriate dose to reduce complications. Severe cases require hospital care for diarrhea with dehydration, pneumonia, or neurologic involvement; infants under 6 months and immunocompromised children need monitoring. Guidance from Dr. Venty of Bethsaida Hospital, Gading Serpong.

articles.summary: Indonesia's Ministry of Health reaffirmed that tuberculosis (TB) is curable with standard anti-TB therapy (OAT), proven safe and effective when administered under healthcare supervision. The regimen—comprising Isoniazid, Rifampicin, Pyrazinamide, and Ethambutol—must be taken consistently for at least six months; interruptions undermine cure and can worsen disease. Officials warn against claims TB can be cured by herbal medicines, noting no scientific evidence supports herbal remedies as a primary TB treatment. Herbal use may only serve as an adjunct to reduce side effects or support immunity. Prof. Dr dr Erlina Burhan, a pulmonologist, stresses that misinformed alternatives can lead patients to seek dangerous options and present with advanced disease. The message, delivered in Jakarta on March 18, 2026, emphasizes adherence to standard OAT to achieve cure.

articles.headlineTranslated: Measles Transmission Could Occur During Eid al-Fitr, a Lecturer from FKIK Unika Atma Jaya Warns of the Importance of Vigilance and Prevention
articles.summary: Measles transmission risk rises during Eid al-Fitr in Indonesia, warns Dr. Regina Satya Wiraharja, Family Medicine lecturer at Unika Atma Jaya. With increased mobility and social mixing, measles cases persist: 2025 laboratory-confirmed cases reached about 11,094 with 69 deaths (CFR ~0.1%), and by week 7 of 2026, 572 cases and 4 deaths, with 13 regions reporting increases. Measles is a highly contagious RNA Morbilivirus infection spread by respiratory droplets; incubation 8–14 days. Early symptoms include high fever, malaise, runny nose, cough, conjunctivitis, and Koplik spots; rash typically appears days 4–14, starting on the face and behind the ears and spreading to the body, lasting 6–7 days. Complications include pneumonia, diarrhea, dehydration, otitis, encephalitis; higher risk for infants, immunocompromised, malnutrition, or vitamin A deficiency. For pregnant women, risks include preterm birth, low birth weight, miscarriage. Prevention: MMR vaccination (9 months, 2 years, 5–6 years), hand hygiene, cough etiquette, masks when symptomatic, and adequate vitamin A. Suspected cases should seek care and limit contact.

As of week 9, 2026, DIY reported 73 laboratory-confirmed measles cases, up 5.6-fold from the same period in 2025, predominantly children aged 2–9 years and infants under 9 months. In Sleman, by February 2026 there were 148 suspected cases, with 33 laboratory-confirmed measles and 4 laboratory-confirmed rubella. Health experts stress the importance of full MR vaccination, especially the second dose, which lags at about 90% coverage, warning that waning immunity could erode herd protection over the next five years. Travelers are advised to consider risks when interacting with babies under 6 months or other vulnerable relatives; avoid crowds if not essential and monitor case trends in destinations. Basic precautions include masking and reducing contact when unwell to curb household spread.

articles.headlineTranslated: Ambacang Public Health Center, Padang City records 34 measles cases in 2025, 5 positive after screening.
articles.summary: Measles outbreak declared at Ambacang Public Health Center, Padang City, after 34 measles cases were recorded in 2025 in the Kuranji district. Of those, five were laboratory-confirmed positive for measles; ten cases were tested, yielding five positives and five negatives. Health authorities state the outbreak status (KLB) is triggered when two positive cases are confirmed, prompting an outbreak response immunization (ORI) campaign conducted in November 2025. Despite negative results in some samples, these cases are treated as measles to halt transmission. In early 2026, 23 measles cases were reported at Ambacang, Anduring, and Kuranji as the year progresses toward Eid al-Fitr 2026. The center continues monitoring and preparing further control measures to curb spread.

articles.headline: Measles Data and the Critical Impact of Global Travel on Disease Resurgence, Highlighting the Intersection of Health and Tourism - Travel And Tour World
articles.summary: Measles remains an exceptionally contagious respiratory virus, with airborne persistence up to two hours. Despite US elimination in 2000, sporadic outbreaks and imported cases persist. CDC reports 2024 had 285 confirmed cases; by March 12, 2026, 1,362 cases across 31 jurisdictions, including California, Florida, New York City, and Texas, with about 94% linked to outbreaks. Most infections occur in unvaccinated or vaccination-unknown individuals. Global travel, international airports, cruise ships, and crowded tourist sites drive transmission, with many cases imported by travelers returning from abroad or visitors, including VFR travelers. Globally, outbreaks are noted in Yemen, India, Indonesia, and Pakistan. Measles can cause pneumonia, encephalitis, and permanent hearing loss; mortality is ~1–3 per 1,000 children. Two-dose MMR is ~97% effective; herd immunity of 95% is needed. Vaccination, laboratory support, diagnostics, and travel guidance from the CDC are critical as travel volumes rise and importation risk remains high.

articles.headlineTranslated: High-end enterovirus vaccine secures drug approval in Vietnam.
articles.summary: Vietnam grants drug approval for High-end's enterovirus 71 (EV71) vaccine, marking the first EV71 vaccine to receive local market authorization and a milestone for Taiwan-originated vaccine exports. The product, submitted in 2023, targets Vietnam's newborn population—about 1.36 million births per year—and addresses a vaccine gap, as no EV71 vaccine is currently available there. With approval, High-end aims to enter the Southeast Asia vaccine market and has signed a regional distribution deal with French firm Substipharm Biologics to develop markets in Thailand, the Philippines, Indonesia, Malaysia, and Singapore. To secure supply for ongoing demand, the company is building a vaccine production line at Zhubei's third biotech campus, planning about NT$871 million in capex to support the existing EV71 vaccine and next-generation products. EV71 is one of the most dangerous enteroviruses for infants and is prevalent in the Asia-Pacific region, with Southeast Asia projected to require millions of doses long-term.

articles.headlineTranslated: A Child Contracts Measles During Eid al-Fitr, Deputy Health Minister Dante: Should Be Isolated, Do Not Gather with Family for Now.
articles.summary: Measles case in Jakarta, Indonesia: A child contracted measles during Eid al-Fitr 2026. Deputy Health Minister Dante Saksono Harbuwono urged parents to isolate the child and avoid family gatherings during Lebaran to cut transmission. The directive was issued at a mudik health post at Gambir Station, Central Jakarta, on March 17, 2026. Measles is highly contagious, with one case capable of infecting 12–18 contacts via respiratory droplets from coughing, sneezing, or talking. Early indicators include fever and skin spots, notably spots on the back of the neck, sometimes with sweating in that area. To prevent spread, families should isolate the child and consider masking when in contact with others during the holiday period. The report highlights the ease of measles transmission and the need for vigilance during travel and Eid celebrations.

articles.headlineTranslated: An immunologist explained what makes childhood impetigo dangerous and how to treat it.
articles.summary: A 3-year-old Russian girl contracted impetigo, a bacterial skin infection, during a vacation in Indonesia. On day 1 she was bitten by mosquitoes, and on day 2 she swam in a warm pool; soon after, skin rashes appeared. Parents initially suspected chickenpox, but physicians diagnosed impetigo. The article features immunologist Nikolai Kryuchkov, who explains what makes childhood impetigo dangerous and how it is treated. It highlights an imported pediatric infection acquired abroad and notes environmental and skin-breach factors that can facilitate bacterial entry. There is no stated laboratory confirmation beyond clinical diagnosis, nor data on case counts or outbreaks. The piece educates on recognition, risk factors, and management of impetigo in children, emphasizing timely treatment to reduce complications and transmission.

articles.headlineTranslated: In addition to biting 11 residents, a rabid cat in Manumutin, Belu Regency also managed to bite a cow.
articles.summary: Rabies outbreak in Manumutin, Kota Atambua, Belu Regency, East Nusa Tenggara, Indonesia: A cat that tested positive for rabies has bitten 11 residents and also bit a cow owned by a local resident. The incident occurred as residents chased the cat near a church in Kelurahan Manumutin. Belu Regency’s Department of Animal Husbandry and Fisheries head Yoos Djami confirmed the report and said a field team has collected a blood sample from the bitten cow to be tested in a laboratory for rabies, assessing possible livestock transmission. Authorities are intensifying control measures, including sweeping for exposed animals, vaccinating animals that can transmit rabies, and monitoring animals suspected of exposure to prevent wider spread. The situation underscores ongoing human exposure and livestock risk while awaiting lab confirmation.

articles.headline: Ceva Animal Health Marks 100 Years of Newcastle Disease Discovery with Global Scientific Gathering in Bogor, Indonesia
articles.summary: Ceva Animal Health marked a century of Newcastle Disease (ND) control with a three-day gathering in Bogor, West Java, Indonesia—the ND birthplace. About 100 participants from 15 countries attended the event "The Guards of a Century - 100 Years with Newcastle Disease." The meeting commemorated ND's 1926 identification in Indonesia and showcased progress in controlling a major avian zoonosis. Key speakers included Dr. Hendra Wibawa (Indonesia Ministry of Agriculture); Prof. Ian Brown (Pirbright Institute); Dr. Kiril Dimitrov (Texas A&M Veterinary Medical Diagnostic Laboratory). Attendees visited Balai Besar Perakitan dan Modernisasi Veteriner, linking discovery to vaccine development. Ceva highlighted its HVTF-based recombinant HVTND vaccine, with Palya showing robust immune responses and Stegeman reporting reduced NDV transmission in broilers. Marcelo Paniago presented trial data showing protection against velogenic genotype VII NDV strains. Ceva reaffirmed its One Health mission and aims for global poultry leadership by 2035.

articles.headline: Penyebab Santri di Jombang Keracunan Terungkap, Ditemukan Nitrit di Telur Asin & Bakteri E. coli
articles.headlineTranslated: Cause of poisoning among santri in Jombang revealed; nitrite found in salted eggs and E. coli bacteria.
articles.summary: Dozens of santri at Pondok Pesantren Sholawat Darut Taubah in Mojoagung District, Jombang Regency, East Java, experienced suspected poisoning. Laboratory tests found nitrite in salted eggs and markedly elevated Escherichia coli in the water used for cooking, drinking, and washing around the pondok. Jombang Health Office head Dr. Hexawan Tjahja Widada said nitrite should not occur in foods, and its presence in salted eggs likely contributed to the acute illness, with symptoms such as nausea and vomiting. E. coli contamination in the water poses risks of gastroenteritis, including abdominal pain, nausea, and diarrhea. Bacillus cereus was also detected in a santri's vomit sample, though investigators are still assessing its link to a food source. Health officials are continuing the investigation to confirm the infection source and whether contaminated water or salted eggs are the primary cause.

articles.headlineTranslated: Bali Health Office on standby at health posts to anticipate measles during mudik
articles.summary: Measles preparedness in Bali during mudik relies on 24/7 health posts at Celukan Bawang and Gilimanuk ports to vaccinate children up to 59 months who are not yet immunized, as a condition for crossing into or continuing travel to Bali. The Bali Health Office (Dinkes) coordinates with local regencies to stock vaccines, with daily demand potentially 2–3 vials (one vial for about 10 children). At health posts, staff interview parents and provide on-site vaccination if needed; surveillance targets symptomatic children (fever and red rash), and samples are collected for confirmation to enable rapid intervention. As of March 2026, 93 suspected measles cases were recorded with 90 specimens tested, yielding no positives; Bali aims to maintain zero measles cases in 2026. In 2025, 109 positive measles cases were reported. Interventions include Outbreak Response Immunization (ORI) and epidemiological investigations, alongside routine surveillance to trigger action for suspected cases.

articles.summary: IDAI (Indonesian Pediatric Society) urges parents to protect children during Lebaran mudik in Indonesia, noting high traveler mobility raises the risk of disease transmission and traffic accidents among the young. Public measures include animal confinement, vaccination of animals, avoiding high-risk animals, and adopting a rabies protocol applicable to dogs, cats, and bats.

articles.headlineTranslated: [Expert Column] Prof. Tjandra Yoga Aditama: Tuberculosis Must Be Treated with Proper Anti-Tuberculosis Therapy.
articles.summary: Five key points by Prof. Tjandra Yoga Aditama emphasize that tuberculosis must be treated with proper anti-tuberculosis therapy (OAT). In response to herbal-therapy claims, he outlines that national and global OAT regimens are defined through three research stages: (1) double-blind case-control trials, (2) multi-center international validation, and (3) expert analysis by WHO and national authorities, ensuring high scientific validity. OAT used in Indonesia and other countries has a long proven track record of cure. While new drugs are under investigation, there is no evidence that herbal treatments can prevent or cure tuberculosis; any such claims must adhere to scientific standards. Misinformation may cause patients to abandon effective OAT, risking non-recovery, disease progression, death, and continued transmission. Switching from proper OAT to inappropriate drugs can drive resistance, including MDR-TB. For accurate information, consult WHO, the Ministry of Health, and professional bodies such as the Indonesian Pulmonologists Association (PDPI).

articles.summary: Rabies outbreak in Belu Regency, East Nusa Tenggara, following a lab-confirmed rabies case from a cat bite that infected 11 residents in Kelurahan Manumutin (Kuneru) on March 14–15, 2026. A coordination meeting led by the Belu Vice Regent approved accelerating vaccination, field surveillance, and risk communication. Vaccine stock is 18,325 doses intended for roughly 36,000 dogs, while Belu’s cat population was about 4,008 in 2025.

articles.headline: Pembangunan 3 juta rumah untuk tekan stunting dan TBC
articles.headlineTranslated: Construction of 3 Million Houses to Curb Stunting and Tuberculosis
articles.summary: Indonesia plans to build 3 million new homes to curb stunting and tuberculosis by improving living conditions in crowded, unhealthy settlements. Announced by Hashim Djojohadikusumo at a Manggarai Station site in Jakarta, the project uses land from PT Kereta Api Indonesia to create healthier, well-ventilated housing. The initiative follows evidence that poor housing contributes to stunting and TB, a major public health challenge, with the Global TB Report 2024 estimating about 1.09 million TB cases and 125,000 TB deaths annually in Indonesia. Health checks have reached 72 million people, yet TB remains prevalent due to sanitation and ventilation gaps. Officials frame housing as a strategic health intervention with broader economic and social equity benefits, referencing international examples (China, Japan, Korea, Singapore) and aligning with TB-focused acceleration efforts highlighted by the Health Ministry in 2025.

articles.headline: Campak en Kalimantan Timur: Baja Cobertura de Vacunación
articles.headlineTranslated: Measles in East Kalimantan: Low Vaccination Coverage.
articles.summary: Measles in East Kalimantan, Indonesia, with vaccination coverage in Samarinda (region known as Bumi Etalase Ibu Kota Nusantara) at 65% for the measles vaccine, well below the national 95% target, leaving about 30% of children unvaccinated and at high risk. As of March 17, 2026, health officials warn that measles is a highly contagious virus causing high fever, cough, runny nose, conjunctivitis, and a red rash, with babies and young children most vulnerable; malnourished adults can also be carriers. To curb transmission, the government has updated the immunization schedule from a single dose to three doses at 9 months, 18 months, and first grade of primary school. 9-month coverage is 62%, 18-month coverage 60%, while first-grade primary school coverage reaches 92%. Cooperation with schools is highlighted as effective, alongside promoting healthy lifestyles to bolster immunity.

articles.headlineTranslated: 282 Mudik Posts in West Java Provide Free Measles Vaccines, Health Department Reminds of Transmission Risk During Eid al-Fitr
articles.summary: West Java's Health Department provides 282 free measles vaccination posts at mudik health posts during Eid al-Fitr 2026 to curb measles transmission amid high population movement. Vaccines are available across mudik posts in all districts and cities of West Java, with stock managed by the provincial health office in collaboration with local puskesmas. If a district/city declares a measles outbreak (KLB), outbreak-management funding is covered by the local government. Most measles cases occur in children with negative or absent vaccination history, underscoring the need for immunization education. Measles is highly contagious and can cause serious complications such as encephalitis, blindness, pneumonia, and severe malnutrition. Health officials urge those with symptoms to isolate, wear masks, and seek prompt care. Nationally, as of February 23, 2026, 8,224 suspected measles cases and 4 deaths; 21 KLB in 17 districts/cities across 11 provinces, led by West Sumatra, South Sumatra, DI Yogyakarta, West Java, and Central Java.
